steps.title: Prepare Blastocyst Lysis Buffer Base
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to prepare 10 ml of Blastocyst Lysis Buffer Base and store at room temperature:

substeps.instruction: Add 2.0 ml of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.3)
Add 2.0 ml of 1 M KCl
Add 40 µl of 2% gelatin
Add 90 µl of Tween 20
Add 5.87 ml of Water

steps.title: Prepare 2X Blastocyst Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to prepare 1 ml of 2X Blastocyst Lysis Buffer and store at -20°C:

substeps.instruction: Add 1.0 ml of Blastocyst Lysis Buffer Base
Add 6.0 µl of 10 mg/ul Yeast tRNA
Add 6.25 µl of 20 mg/ml Proteinase K
Add Water to reach final volume

steps.title: Prepare 5X CES Solution
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to prepare 1 ml of 5X Combinatorial PCR Enhancer Solution (CES) and store at -20°C:

substeps.instruction: Add 540 µl of 5M Betaine
Add 6.7 µl of 1M DTT
Add 67.0 µl of DMSO
Add 157.1 µl of 35% BSA
Add 229.2 µl of Water

steps.title: Lyse Blastocysts and Store Lysate
steps.instruction: Perform blastocyst lysis to produce a crude DNA preparation:

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µl of 2X Blastocyst Lysis Buffer to each blastocyst frozen in a PCR tube
Place PCR tubes in a thermal cycler
Run the following program: 56°C for 10 min, 95°C for 10 min, then 4°C indefinitely
Store the resulting crude lysate at -20°C

steps.title: Design PCR Primers
steps.instruction: Use Primer-Blast (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/tools/primer-blast) to design primers with the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Set Minimum primer melting temperature to 60°C
Set Optimal primer melting temperature to 63°C
Set Maximum primer melting temperature to 66°C
Set Minimum primer melting temperature difference to 1°C
Enable 'search for primer pairs specific to the intended PCR template'
Set Search Mode to 'Automatic'
Set Database to 'Genomes for selected eukaryotic organisms (primary assembly only)'
Set Organism to 'Mus musculus (taxid:10090)'
Set Primer Minimum size to 14
Set Primer Optimum size to 29
Set Primer Maximum size to 31

steps.title: Perform Blastocyst PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the target DNA segment using the crude blastocyst DNA:

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µl PCR reaction containing 4 µl of crude blastocyst DNA
Add primers, Taq polymerase (KOD polymerase is recommended if others fail), PCR reaction buffer, and water to reach 20 µl
For inefficient reactions, use a buffer with final concentrations: 65 mM Tris–HCl, 16.6 mM (NH4)2SO4, 3.1 mM MgCl2, and 0.01% (v/v) Tween 20 at pH 8.8
Run the PCR program: 98°C for 2 minutes (initial denaturing), Tm -2°C for 30 seconds (annealing), 72°C for 30 seconds (extension), and 95°C for subsequent denaturing steps
Perform 35-40 cycles, then hold at 4°C indefinitely

steps.title: Analyze PCR Products
steps.instruction: Examine the amplification results and validate the process:

substeps.instruction: Run the PCR products on a 1% agarose gel to check for a single band of the expected size
Run a negative control (water template) to ensure no background contaminating DNA
If no bands are detected, optimize primers using a 20 µl PCR reaction with 50 pg DNA to simulate blastocyst conditions
